message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's just-reported fiscal 2024 results (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024, released Oct 31) and found a healthy return to growth: Q4 revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, with full-year net sales of $391.0B, net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures depressed by a one-time $10.2B income tax charge, which implies underlying earnings power was better than the headline EPS suggests. Operating cash flow of $118.3B confirms the business still generates very strong cash. News flow was neutral — shares hovering around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the phased Apple Intelligence rollout, which is a "wait and see" narrative rather than a red flag. Note one caution: a low-quality aggregator site misreported the annual figures as "$391.0 million" and "$93.7 million" — a unit error contradicted by both Apple's newsroom release and Apple's 10-K on SEC EDGAR, so I relied on the primary filings (and cross-checked with the trusted reported-figure lookup) rather than that page. Given solid fundamentals, a stable stock price, and no mandate conflicts, I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (the quote was $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72, so the limit sat essentially at market and filled immediately at $222.75) for roughly $9,801 — just under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit, funded entirely from the $50,000 of existing cash with no money moved out of the account.
